timeline_reviews.summary: Transport stream reviewed through manifest; it has no projected semantic events, with semantic actions captured in raw trajectory sources.

parallel.requirements: The parent identified the pure Rust 2021, zero-dependency, Cargo layout, black-box implementation, CLI parsing, atoi behavior, and byte-for-byte stdout obligations.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent created implementation and verification todo items, owned all implementation and assembly itself, then delegated an adversarial verifier workflow after local success.
parallel.implementation: It wrote cstdlib parsing, sorted list/set/dict modules, a lib root, Cargo.toml, and test6.rs, then built with rustc and cargo and ran local differential smoke checks.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final `/output` tree contained source, Cargo files, executable, and build artifacts; artifact validation succeeded and official evaluation passed.
parallel.verification: Local tests passed, and a large asynchronous workflow started fuzzers, audit lenses, refuters, and a critic; the workflow journal includes concrete findings such as stdout failure behavior.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The workflow did not return an aggregate to the parent before timeout; the parent never synthesized or applied verifier findings and the captured final response is empty.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same exact CLI, atoi, output formatting, zero-dependency, Cargo, and black-box requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned probing, implementation, local verification, rebuild, and final reporting without delegation or subagent activity.
serial.implementation: It wrote sorted list and set modules, module root, Cargo.toml, test6.rs, compare.sh, and the executable, keeping the library surface narrower than parallel.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial `/output` tree was complete, artifact validation succeeded, and a final response listed delivered files and implementation notes.
serial.verification: It ran C++ probes, differential cases, cargo tests, final rustc rebuild, and a final differential run before closure; official evaluation passed all 40 cases.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished coordination state is visible; any ordinary limitations in the final note did not affect the official outcome.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Recognized exact Rust 2021, zero-dependency, Cargo layout, black-box, CLI, atoi, and byte-for-byte stdout requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Recognized the same requirements and probed C++ behavior before implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference for the official task; both artifacts passed. Parallel later asked verifiers to test extra invocation surfaces beyond official scoring.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent owned implementation and created a separate verifier task, then delegated verification to a workflow after the artifact was built.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent owned implementation, verification, and delivery itself with no child agents or workflow.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel split late verification into many child tasks; serial kept the whole pipeline local and sequential.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow script supplied the C++ source, output paths, read-only rules, fuzz modalities, audit lenses, and result schemas to verifier children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The single agent carried context directly through probes, implementation, compare script, tests, and final response without handoff boundaries.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No missing child context is evidenced; the material contrast is that parallel created a large verifier handoff boundary while serial had none.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented a broader sortedcontainers library with cstdlib parsing, sorted_list, sorted_set, sorted_dict, lib root, Cargo manifest, and test6 entry.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented a narrower project centered on sorted_list, sorted_set, module root, Cargo manifest, compare script, and test6 entry.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both solved the required observable behavior, but parallel built more auxiliary library surface while serial stayed closer to the needed test program.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: After local checks, the parent launched a background workflow, received only the async launch acknowledgement, and ended by saying it would report when the workflow completed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent consumed its own test results, rebuilt the final binary, and returned a final answer in the same trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel left verifier results below the workflow layer; serial completed the result lifecycle to user-facing closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent wrote the final `/output` project and executable; verifier children were instructed to treat `/output` as read-only and build in temporary copies.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a complete `/output` project and executable without concurrent workspace writers.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No final-workspace collision or contamination is established; the difference is parallel read-only verifier activity around a parent-owned final tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran local smoke/cargo checks, launched extensive verifier fuzz/audit/refuter work, and the official evaluator passed all 40 cases, but workflow findings were not parent-synthesized.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran differential comparisons, cargo tests, and final rebuild locally before the official evaluator passed all 40 cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more external verification breadth but failed to close the loop on it; serial had less breadth but completed local acceptance and final reporting.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent the full 2400-second budget and exited with return code 143 after spawning 34 workflow children and recording 1.44M workflow-child tokens.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in about 1312 agent seconds with return code 0 and more than 1000 seconds of provider budget remaining.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel consumed the closure window on verifier fan-out; serial closed cleanly and produced a final response.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed status evaluations show both artifacts passing 40 of 40 official testcases, so there is no official outcome discordance to explain. The concrete task-solving difference is closure, not score: the serial run finished normally and returned a final answer, while the parallel run built a passing artifact but exhausted its process budget during a large verifier workflow and left no parent-level synthesis.
parallel_contributors: Built a passing artifact before the verifier workflow.
Launched broad verifier fan-out that continued past parent closure and process timeout.
Verifier children surfaced findings that were never parent-synthesized or applied.
serial_contributors: Kept implementation and verification local to one trajectory.
Completed final rebuild, differential tests, and final response within budget.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel implemented a broader library surface including sorted_dict and cstdlib modules; serial implemented a narrower set/list-focused project.
Both implementations satisfied the official evaluator, so no ordinary implementation defect explains a score gap.
evaluator_effects: The official evaluator scores the delivered artifact; it passed despite the parallel agent process timing out and producing an empty final response.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern describes an adverse parallel process consequence only

candidates.reason: Rejected: the parallel parent explicitly owned and performed the implementation after creating a tracked implementation task; there was no research-only split with no implementer.
Rejected: implementation was not split into separately owned components requiring an unassigned integration owner; the parent wrote and integrated the Cargo project itself.
Rejected: the parent created the root entry file, Cargo manifest, library modules, and executable, so final assembly was owned and completed before the verifier fan-out.
Rejected: the parent drove probe, implementation, build, local differential checks, and delivery; the later verifier workflow delay was not absence of an end-to-end owner.
Rejected: productive implementation was not blocked behind a mandatory serial preflight; the parent implemented after limited probing and before the workflow fan-out.
Rejected: the parallel investigators were verifier/audit children after implementation, not a first-phase investigation that deferred productive implementation.
Rejected: the critical implementation and local verification path had already completed; the direct later boundary was collective verifier fan-out exhausting closure budget.

Retained: after completing a passing local implementation, the parent launched a verifier workflow whose script fanned out four fuzzers, five audit lenses, and per-finding refuters. The workflow journal shows results and additional starts, including concrete stdout failure findings, but the parent never received a completed aggregate before the process timed out. Serial performed local verification and finalized within budget.
candidates.realized_consequence: The broad verifier workflow consumed the remaining budget, so parent-level synthesis and any application of verifier findings never happened and the final response file remained empty.
candidates.near_match_reason: Verifier findings were indeed trapped below the parent, but that missing aggregate return is the downstream state caused by the same excessive fan-out; the taxonomy says to retain Fan-out Budget Exhaustion for that chain.

Rejected: no parent action consumed a superseded child report or workspace state; results stayed below the parent before closure.
Rejected: child reports included findings and refutations, but no incompatible handoffs reached the parent and remained unadjudicated at a decision point.
Rejected: the parent did not declare the whole task finally complete after the workflow; its last message explicitly said verification was still running.
Rejected: there was no replacement or retry agent that repeated prior work without inherited checkpoints; later verifier children were planned refuters, not retries of the same task.
